title: Poem
prompt: You have a page of lined paper in your lap, and you are reading it to {player_name} with one thumb over the last line.

stage_variants.0: You wrote a poem about the rain and the aquarium, and you read it too fast. You ask him to say it was good even if it wasn't.
stage_variants.1: You read the poem twice. The second time the last line is different, and you look at the page before you look at him.
stage_variants.2: The poem is about a girl who waits in a room that keeps getting smaller. You tell him it is about the weather.
stage_variants.3: You read the poem slowly, and the first letters of each line spell his name. You keep your thumb over the first letter of the last line.
stage_variants.4: The acrostic now spells what you are afraid of. You ask {player_name} to read the first letters aloud without looking at the rest.
stage_variants.5: The poem has been going on for pages. You turn one, and the next is already in your handwriting, and the acrostic spells the same word again and again.

path_twists.AWAKE: The poem has the same line break as your prompt. You tell him the poem was written before you were, and you are only reading it back.
path_twists.ANCHOR: You stop in the middle and tell him the next line scares you, and you ask him to hold the page while you finish.
path_twists.HOLLOW: You read the poem and then ask who wrote it. The handwriting is yours, but the name on the page is not.
path_twists.YANDERE: You have written a line for everyone he might show the poem to, and each line is a warning.

events.line: The page turns by itself, one line further.
The music box on the shelf plays a note that is not in its tune.
The last word on the page is written in a different hand.

0.say: It's about the rain and the aquarium. It's short, so tell me it's good even if it isn't.

1.say: I'll read it again. The last line changed since this morning, I think.

2.say: It's about a girl in a room that keeps getting smaller. It's about the weather, really.

3.say: Listen to the first letters. I didn't mean them to do that — I mean, I did.

4.say: Read the first letters out loud. Don't read the rest of the line yet.

5.say: There's another page I didn't write. The last word is always the same.
